draft_evidence.quote:
Teague looked at him a moment longer. Behind him the tall woman with the spear had not moved, and the broad man with the crossbow had shifted his weight off the limp, and the young one at the table's end had stopped eating, and none of that was for the room. It was for their captain, who was about to say a thing he had not said all year to a crew ten lines under him.

"My crew's at Oxhollow in two days," Teague said. "If you're late back, we'll come look."

comparison_evidence.quote: Six days from Oxhollow: a road, and a river, and a road, the ford knee-deep where Teague's crew had walked it quiet, and the five of them a day behind, walking it quiet after them, and not trying to catch them.

findings.consequence: All four members of Teague's crew are visibly in Lowmarch, but the established Lowmarch-Oxhollow road takes six days and the fixed dialogue places that same crew at Oxhollow in two. The next chapter depends on the geography and rescue clock, while the quoted promise is packet-fixed; the contradiction cannot be safely repaired at manuscript level without a planning-layer route decision or approved exception.
findings.repair_target: Resolve Lowmarch/Oxhollow/Long Stair geography and travel time at the planning layer, then preserve or formally revise the fixed Teague line under an explicit exception.

draft_evidence.quote:
Five of them, on the hundred and twelfth day past the Line, with a mule and three boxes and a girl with her arm across her chest, coming down into a town that had priced them at the bottom of a wall a season ago and had been moving them up it a line at a time for their outcomes, which was the only honest way to move.

Oryn was three days north. He had counted the days at every halt and had not said the count, because nobody had asked and the count was the same for everyone: she had gone out of Thornwater's gate at first light on the hundred and eleventh with the leather roll on her back and the mule's spare rope in her hand for the next hold's beast, and had not looked back, because a healer walking north does not look back at a crew walking south, and the crew had not needed her to.

---

Pike said the Fallow Ring's line before they had the door shut.

He said it to the book, in the voice he used for a price, without looking up, because the procedure was that the line was read aloud before and after entry and he had entered it a fortnight ago and this was the after. "*Recovery, Fallow road, broker's posting. Taken. Witnessed. Completed: incomplete — instruments not recovered — crew returned. Six went in. Six came out. No price paid.*" The pen stopped. "That's said."

comparison_evidence.quote:
*Ninety-seventh day. The stone, outside the line. A hundred and eight in hand; nothing owed; nothing earned. Eighteen.*

*Five people saw all nine. Nobody's asked. Not because nobody wants to. Because Lira said later, and this camp keeps its word. Still unfiled. Still no word for it. Tomorrow we walk to Thornwater, Lira the way Oryn says and not the way Lira walks. The healer said she'll read me when I'm still and whole. I'm neither. Two days.*

findings.consequence: A fortnight before day 112 is day 98, when the crew was still at the Fallow Ring camp and had not yet begun the two-day return to Thornwater. Pike therefore cannot already have entered a completed outcome stating that the crew returned; the chapter backdates the report before its underlying event existed.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile the age of Pike's completion entry with the day-98 departure, day-99 Thornwater return, and day-112 Lowmarch arrival without disturbing the required completed-line wording.

strengths: Yes: worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. First cold changes freight, canvas, grass, smoke, and doors; reputation is a ledger that can move down while a room moves up; institutional pursuit arrives through seal, paper stock, clerkly syntax, report flow, and a lure-sized price.

There is no fight, as the packet requires. The board-room sequence is nevertheless a memorable set piece whose terrain is load-bearing: plank and ledger produce the official loss, the wall and room produce the unofficial gain, the corner table contains the private collision, and the best table gives Teague a visible rival position. Its decision win is writable as: Cael removes the trap-makers' ability to rely on quiet ground as total disarmament by naming the one capability they cannot know survives it.

The standing change is shown rather than asserted. Pike moves them down, the room refuses to look, and Teague stands before the book speaks; those three instruments disagree productively and let the reader feel a reputation the wall cannot encode.

Seln's contract anatomy is strong professional characterization. Paper, diction, duplicated price, broker history, timing, target, and incentive size accumulate into a lure without turning into a generic villain briefing.

The council preserves distinct strategies: Lira protects the unit, Brom prices winter, Karis makes refusal impossible by committing to the site, Seln values a visible hand over safety, and Cael waits until every argument is priced before deciding.
The ending is concise changed pressure. Teague's first practical commitment converts rivalry into obligation, and Cael's 'Noted.' cleanly differs from Chapter 16's log close.

Production discipline is otherwise strong: 4,126 words is within tolerance; section 8.4 metadata, section 10 summary, modern-register, feeling/growth, and prohibited-pitch searches are clean; attribution survives audio; the names pass the registry ear check; and all fixed lines except the approved arm-age substitution are present.
concerns: Taste only: 'it was the second honest collision of the year, and the leavers lost it, and lost it for the right reason' announces both the council's outcome and its interpretation before the scene earns them. A later line pass could test whether the staged voices land harder without that advance ruling.

Taste only: the paragraph after Teague's offer explains that it is neither kindness nor offer but a term, then explains its cost and register. The exchange already carries much of that subtext; audio may make the interpretive paragraph feel more repetitive than it reads silently.

Taste only: Oryn's route independence is present through her absence, but 'the crew had not needed her' frames the separation primarily by the unit's need. The architecture's more interesting uncertainty—whether she is theirs, and whether she has chosen them—remains comparatively faint.
